Understand the estimate

We divide forecast state residential electricity sales by the assumed number of residential accounts, then adjust using a survey-weighted home-type and floor-area group.

Size is grouped into bands. Homes in the same type and size band receive the same adjustment. When a state group is too small, we use its region or the U.S. and show that here.

Annual patterns from 2020 are applied to a monthly forecast. Actual use also depends on heating, weather, occupancy, appliances and behaviour. No household prediction interval has been validated.

FROM DATA TO DECISIONS

Understand your estimate.

Your location, home type and size provide a starting point for electricity planning.

01

Choose your location

Select a state and an available month. We start with forecast electricity use per residential account in that state.

02

Describe your home

Choose your home type and your own home's floor area. A survey-weighted comparison group adjusts the state average for that profile.

03

Explore the estimate

See the monthly planning estimate, compare it with the state average, and check the number and location of supporting survey homes.

THE HOUSEHOLD SCENARIO

State forecast (MWh) × 1,000 ÷ residential accounts × home-profile factor

The home-profile factor is a weighted survey group mean divided by its geographic reference mean.

Data you can trace

  • 10,200 state-month source observations
  • 50 states and Washington, D.C.
  • 17,851 survey profiles after excluding known solar homes
  • 153 saved state-month forecasts

Designed for transparency

The web app uses a fixed research snapshot through August 2026. Available estimate months are September–November 2026. It does not automatically ingest new utility data.

Survey weights support profile comparisons. Small groups fall back to broader geography. Unsupported profiles receive no estimate.

HomePulse is a student project by Ghaida Aljuhani for MIT 1.125. It is not an EIA product.
